White Bean Soup with Sage

Serves 6 to 8

% cup (120 ml) extra-virgin olive oil, plus
additional for drizzling
2% medium red onions, halved, then sliced
lengthwise Yi inch (6 mm) thick

6 large garlic cloves, peeled and minced

7 cups (1,587 g) cooked white beans

3 cups (750 ml) warm water

1 tablespoon (15 g) plus 1 teaspoon (5 g) sea salt

2 pinches freshly ground black pepper

Ya teaspoon (1 g) crushed red pepper
Y pound (220 g) stale country bread, cubed
Ys inch (1.5 cm) wide and toasted

12 fresh sage leaves

Warm the olive oil in a heavy 6-quart (6 L)
soup pot over medium heat. Once it shimmers,
add the onions and garlic. Sauté, stirring often,
until the onions are limp and pale gold, about 12

minutes.

Add the beans. Swirl the water around the
bean pot, tip it in, and bring the soup
up to a simmer; stir to combine
Add the salt and pepper. Cook for 15 minutes on
medium heat, stirring so nothing catches.

Add the crushed red pepper and the toasted bread,
pressing the cubes under the surface.
Turn the heat to low and leave the soup for 15
minutes. Tear the sage leaves
into the pot; stir them through, and cook for
another 5 minutes.

To finish, ladle into warm wide bowls, making sure
everyone gets some of the bread.
Pour a thread of extra-virgin olive oil over
each bowl and serve at once,

Opposite, above: Nonna, Lia Ferri, and
Sandro. Below: Tessa,
